title: GS21 with the priced y factor on production, exposure = standardized PRODUCTIVITY (gvyz10), and a FIXED capital structure: three leverage types with the coupon per unit capital held at 0.158, 0.421, 0.684 by monthly costless refinancing (xi = 1, kappa_b = 0), drawn independently of productivity
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when the exposure is a PRODUCT of a hidden type and a within-firm state, so the premium is an interaction the ranks cannot span?
notes: 2026-10-22. gvyzl's five finished seeds showed the fixed-coupon types leak: the coupon is diluted by 1/g at every investment and resets only at a refinancing opportunity (xi = 1% a month), so the realized coupon per unit capital had median 0.17 and p90 0.36 against set-points 0.16/0.42/0.68, and leverage still rank-correlated 0.94 with book-to-market. Here the firm refinances every month (xi = 1) at its type's coupon with no issuance cost (kappa_b = 0), so debt scales with capital and leverage is the type: the capital structure is exogenous and fixed. Everything else gvyz10's.

changes: gs_bv [0.1, 0.1, 0.1] x (gs_bzl 0.0 + gs_bzi 1.0 z~): type x productivity exposure, bv_comp 0.0
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

method.gs_vy_exposure: production x exp(gs_bv (gs_bzl + gs_bzi z~) y)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
